sentences.text: This appeal is directed against the judgment and order of acquittal passed by the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Chandrapur on 08.07.1997 in Regular Criminal Case No. 40/1998 by which the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate acquitted the respondent of the offence punishable under Sections 16(i) (a) (ii), 16 (1) (a) (i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.

2. The record shows that when this appeal came up for final hearing after admission on 25.03.2009,
this Court heard the 2 apeal429.97.odt learned A.P.P. for the State and decided the matter in absence of the learned counsel for the respondent thereby upsetting the judgment and order of acquittal.

3. The respondent, feeling aggrieved, approached the Hon'ble Apex Court by filing the Criminal Appeal No.2276/2009 and the Hon'ble Apex Court vide judgment dated 09.09.2015 upset the judgment delivered by this Court on the ground that the appeal filed on behalf of the State ought not The State Of Maharashtra vs Shri Ramchabila Jagnath Yadav on 4 July, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67037969/
1 to have been proceeded with in the absence of learned counsel for the respondent and therefore the matter was remanded back to this Court for deciding it afresh.

sentences.text: 4. I have heard Mr. R. S. Nayak, learned A.P.P. for the State and Mr. S. V. Sirpurkar, learned counsel for the respondent.

5. A charge was framed against the respondent by the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate for an offence punishable under Sections 16(i) (a) (ii), 16 (1) (a) (i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act for contravening the provisions of Rule 15 of the Rules made under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 3 apeal429.97.odt 1955 and thereby the respondent was charged that he has committed an offence punishable under Sections 16(i) (a) (ii), 16 (1) (a) (i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.
6.

entities.text: Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 3 apeal429.97.odt 1955
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Ashok Patait, Food Inspector, had on 23.04.1987 found that the respondent was selling milk from a can which was attached to his motorcycle.
Since Ashok Patait, Food Inspector was intending to take the sample of that milk, he purchased 750 ml. of buffalo milk by paying price of Rs.2/- after obtaining receipt from the respondent.
The milk, which was purchased from the can was obtained after stirring the contents thereof in well manner.
Thereafter the sample was divided in 3 parts.
After adding 20 drops of Formalin in the bottle as preservative, the sample was duly sealed.
The samples were sent to the Local Health authority.
A sample bottle was also forwarded to Public Analyst who found that the sample is not in conformity with the standards.
The Public Analyst's report is at Exh.-34 which was communicated to the Food Inspector by Covering Letter Exh.-33.
The report shows that the sample contains total solids of 10.53%, milk fat 4%, solids not fat 6.33%.
According to the rules, the milk should have milk fats 6%, the milk solid in fat 9%.
It is also found 4 apeal429.97.odt during the investigation that the respondent was not having any license for selling the milk.
After obtaining consent from the Joint Commissioner of Food and Drug Administration, a complaint was filed before the learned Magistrate.
A perusal of the record shows that the notice was also given to the respondent that he has right if he wants to challenge the report of the Public Analyst from Central Food Laboratory at Gaziabad.
Though it was made known by the complainant to the accused about his statutory rights, the respondent failed to exercise his statutory right.
Therefore, the report Exh.-34 given by the Public Analyst reached to its finality.
7. It appears that the learned Magistrate has acquitted the accused by observing in paragraph 18 of the impugned judgment that the samples were not taken after stirring the contents of the can.
Such an observation of the learned Magistrate is totally contrary to the evidence that is brought on record.

It would be useful to reproduce the version of the complainant which is as under:
"The 750 ml. Of milk was purchased by me from the can containing 20 Ltrs. Of buffalo milk after stirring the same well."
5
apeal429.97.odt
Further, there is no challenge to this particular version during the course of cross-examination of the complainant.

In spite of this evidence available on record, the learned Magistrate has observed in paragraph 18, which in my view, is contrary and he has not read the evidence properly, resulting into a perverse approach on his part while deciding the criminal case.

2 8.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Though the prosecution did not examine the panch witness, the prosecution cannot be blamed since before starting of the evidence, he was dead.
There was no reason for the learned Magistrate to disbelieve the evidence of Patait (PW1) the complainant.
Learned counsel for the respondent could not point out from the evidence as brought on record any procedural lapses on the part of the complainant while collecting the samples.

Since the learned Magistrate has not considered the evidence available on record and has recorded a finding of fact which is contrary to the facts established on record, in my view, the judgment has resulted in miscarriage of justice.
9. Resultantly, the appeal is allowed.
The judgment and 6 apeal429.97.odt order dated 08.07.1997 passed by Chief Judicial Magistrate in Regular Criminal Case No.40/1988 acquitting the respondent is set aside.

The respondent is convicted for the offence punishable under Sections 16(i) (a) (ii), 16 (1) (a) (i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and he is directed to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 3 months and to pay a fine of Rs.500/-.
The respondent is entitled to set off under Section 428 of the Cr. P. C. for the period for which he has already undergone the sentence.
The respondent is granted 8 weeks' time to surrender to his bail bonds.
